To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Venture capital (VC) firms that enjoy more powerful positions within the network of relationships among VC firms have significantly better fund investment performance, as measured in terms of the proportion of investments successfully exited.

(1) the network of VC firms has a significant influence on the performance of VC funds; (2) the network of a VC firm has a significant influence over the survival of its portfolio companies; (3) the network of the VC firm has a significantly positive influence over the exit of its portfolio companies, and; (4) VC networks evolve in response to the performance of the VC firms in the network, with better performing VC firms gaining more influential positions.
VC firms that are better networked enjoy superior fund performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance implications of network relationships in financial markets.
the performance implications of network relationships in the VC industry, an area that has been largely unexplored in previous research.

a central question in the field of VC finance: How does the network of relationships among VC firms and between VC firms and their portfolio companies affect the success of VC firms, the performance of the companies in which they invest, and ultimately the performance of the funds they manage?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VC networks are a key factor in determining the success of the portfolio company investments and the performance of the venture capital fund.
the network position of the VC firm is a key factor in explaining the performance of both the firm and its investments.
venture capital networks and their influence on investment performance are important and should be studied further.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VC networks matter, and that they are a significant source of value for VC funds and their portfolio companies.
venture capitalists who are more central in a network of relationships have better performance.
VC network position matters, but the effect is more complex than the simple notion that the more connected you are, the better your outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
network positions matter in the VC industry and that they are a significant source of value for VC firms and their portfolio companies.
VC networks are important for understanding the VC industry, and that the performance of VC funds depends on their position in the network.
the structure of VC networks is an important determinant of VC fund and portfolio company performance, and that network positions can change over time as the industry evolves.
